safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.5 to 1.48 days

narrative: Material PL1__M290AAB3 shows stable, high-volume daily demand (~1,007 units/day) with moderate variability (CV=0.25) and a mild upward trend. Lead times are short (mean 1.59 days) but volatile (CV=0.53), which together with demand variability produces a sigma_LTD of 907 units. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is selected because demand is near-continuous and the EOQ (8,999) comfortably exceeds the MOQ of 200 without breaching the 14,728-unit storage cap. Safety stock must be increased from 669 to 1,492 units to achieve the 95% service level target.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous and non-zero every working day, making a continuous-review (r,Q) model optimal. The EOQ far exceeds the MOQ, confirming fixed-cost-driven ordering is appropriate. No intermittency or lumpy demand patterns were observed that would require a base-stock or Croston-type model.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilization is 71.2% (10,491 of 14,728 units), leaving adequate headroom. No capacity cap binding. If demand trend continues upward, storage may become binding within 12-18 months — monitor.
